about: Documented GTK limits (docs/developer/kit/lumaui-deviations.md) that lumaui-conform reports as 'accepted' instead of failing. Each entry is narrow: optional states, group, subject and prop regexes, and max_delta (the largest difference it forgives). Add one only with a matching row in lumaui-deviations.md.

deviations.reason: Island fill = shell island material: the status island's fill is the Shell's own island material, and the reference's placeholder fill was never part of the design (layer permissions, review 1). The cell compare covers the cell's own pixels: the icons with their 1.5-2 px violet rings, the stack and the +N square. The 3 px separation ring outside them is rgba(0,0,0,.35) over the island, so it shows the island material and is masked with it.
Antialiasing of the 16 px icons, their whole-pixel rings and the 9 px +N on the cell; accepted only while the mean ΔE over the cell's own pixels stays at or under 3 (layer permissions, review 1).

The Shell's translucent material is canonical (layer permissions, review 3 and the standard-banner ruling of 22 Nov): the banner's surface (over the home screen on a phone), its button fills (white at 10% over the banner) and the badge ring are translucent material, which the reference does not draw. The offer is compared over its content only, in every posture: the icon and badge art, the text and the button labels.

The offer is the Shell's standard banner (review 2): its tile and Settings badge are art (review 5) and its buttons are the banner's own controls, whose fills are material (22 Nov ruling); both are left out of the fill-heat check, the mean still counts them. Same rule as the app-permissions folder offer.

The banner's actions are content-width: each button's width follows its label's advance, which differs between Pango and Chromium (the desktop ruling of 22 Nov, Not now about 1 px wider, an edge). At TV scale (x1.5) that difference puts the button edges a little over the 5% edge check.
As translucent-shell-material: the TV popover is the Shell's translucent material over the wallpaper; compared over its content only.

Chromium and Pango break and antialias the banner's body differently: at the 314 px line Chromium carries "2 apps" of the partial result to its second line, where the shell keeps it on the first, and the continued notice's dark-on-light text differs by its antialiasing. Only these two light states' fill heat may reach 0.75 %; their mean and every other state are judged as built.

Spec section 1: the install sheet's header (icon, name, kind, publisher) stays as Valet has it, and so does the main column's surface (its recessed card under the app's lit header wash, as the targets show); the reference page draws its own header on a flat window fill. The sheet is compared over its permission blocks: the headings, the three cards, the chips, the device request, the Never line and the review strip (on a phone and a TV: the facts, headings and lists).

As translucent-shell-material (layer permissions, review 3 item 3): the folder offer is the Shell's standard banner, whose material shows what is behind it and is canonical; the reference draws an opaque card. The surface is masked: compared over its content only (the app's tile and badge, the source, time, title and body each as wide as its words, and the two buttons), on every posture.

Review 3 (as the mixer slider): LumaUI's real controls are canonical for #537, the radio dot's accent, the switch and button rims. Their pixels are left out of the fill-heat check; the mean still counts them.
Review 1: the shell's banner placement, type, badge and Not now width are accepted as built; the banner's buttons are left out of the fill-heat check, the mean still counts them.

Review 3: the page's top hue wash is Settings' own material and is masked, as shell material is: Settings is compared over its content (the header, hero, groups and notes), not the page surface around them, and the scenario leaves the wash's band (the island's top 300 px, where it also shows through the light cards) out of every score.

Review 3 ruling: light Settings' all-files card below the masked wash band leaves only its bottom rim in the fill check; the ~27 hot pixels are that 1 px rim after a 1 px alignment slip, which counts as an edge.

Review rulings: TV is the desktop at x1.5, so 1-2 px rims become up to 3 px. The tile's sub-pixel edge ring at x1.5 is a rim (scenario material: art ring 1.5 px each side), and Not now's slightly wider box with its designed focus ring are edges (edge pixels over ΔE 10 up to 10%).

On a phone the lip's translucent material shows the home screen's widgets through the buttons' rims, so their edge pixels measure the backdrop, not the geometry. The buttons' boxes are checked by position instead (Allow at 60,76 and Not now at 123,76 within 1 px of the reference, anchored on the tile); their edge colour is not judged.
